title: Bomb Tester
intro: Kwiat's interaction-free bomb test, unrolled. Each amber plate turns the polarization by 22.5°, so after all four a horizontal photon would arrive vertical and miss the horizontal analyzer at the target. A bomb station is a polarizing beam splitter whose vertical port leads into the bomb: horizontal passes, vertical sets the bomb off. Each station sends the photon back to horizontal at the cost of sin² of the small angle turned since the last look. Stations fit in the gaps between plates, never inside one. Place them so the photon reaches the target having 'seen' the bomb without touching it: one look per cycle; a second look in the same gap sees nothing new.
goal: Place bomb stations in the gaps between the amber plates so the photon reaches the target still horizontal without setting off the bomb.

physics.point: Each bomb station asks 'horizontal?', and a 'yes' undoes the plates' turn. A photon that arrives horizontal proves the bomb is there, yet it never touched it.

idea: Each amber plate turns the polarization by 22.5°. Four of them turn horizontal into vertical, and the horizontal analyzer at the target blocks vertical.

A bomb station passes horizontal and sends vertical into the bomb. After one plate the photon is at 22.5°. With probability cos²22.5° ≈ 0.85 it passes and is exactly horizontal again; otherwise the bomb goes off.

With a station in every gap the photon keeps being reset and arrives horizontal more than half the time. Without a bomb there would be no stations, and it would arrive vertical. So a horizontal photon at the target reveals the bomb, and that photon never entered the bomb's port.

This is Kwiat's version of the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb test, laid out in a line. With more, smaller steps the success probability approaches 1. The level shows only the world with the bomb; removing all stations shows the world without it.
maths: Three stations in the three gaps plus the analyzer at the target make four looks, each after a 22.5° turn:
The remaining 0.091 arrives vertical and misses. Two stations in one gap and none in another gives a 45° step, and cos²45° = ½:
With N steps of 90°/N the law is cos²ᴺ(90°/N), which tends to 1 as N grows.

Measured as a share of what reaches the target with no plates (32%): 0.48 with one station per gap (ideal 0.53) and 0.34 doubled up (ideal 0.36); booms 0.41 (ideal 0.38). The packet's 11% speed spread blurs each plate's angle. P<sub>T</sub> ≈ 15% for one station per gap.

A fourth station after the last plate leaves P<sub>T</sub> unchanged and turns the vertical leftover into booms (0.41 → 0.48). One before the first plate does nothing: the photon is still horizontal there.
try: Remove all stations: the photon arrives vertical and P<sub>T</sub> ≈ 1%. This is the world without a bomb.
Place one station in each of the three gaps between plates: P<sub>T</sub> ≈ 15%, while the bomb goes off in about 41% of runs (the P<sub>M</sub> meter).
Put two stations in the first gap and one in the second, leaving the third gap empty: P<sub>T</sub> falls to about 11%.
